articles.title: Jusqu'à 30 gigaoctets par heure : le bug silencieux des pilotes Nvidia GeForce qui fatigue votre SSD — Frandroid
articles.summary:
Il y a quelques jours, AMD a reconnu que ses pilotes Radeon écrivaient sans arrêt sur le SSD, même quand le PC ne fait rien, puis a publié un correctif dans la foulée. Les possesseurs de cartes graphiques GeForce ne sont visiblement pas à l’abri : dans un article publié ce mercredi 18 novembre, le site américain Wccftech rassemble des témoignages d’utilisateurs dont les pilotes
Nvidia écrivent eux aussi en continu sur le disque système, et dit avoir reproduit le problème sur l’une de ses machines. Ça compte, parce qu’un SSD ne supporte qu’un volume limité d’écritures sur sa durée de vie : chaque gigaoctet écrit pour rien l’use un peu plus.
Un vieux bug que les derniers pilotes aggravent
En cause, NVDisplay.Container.exe, un processus qui tourne en arrière-plan pour le service NVIDIA Display Container LS, dont le panneau de configuration Nvidia et l’application NVIDIA App ont besoin pour fonctionner. D’après les rapports d’utilisateurs, ce processus réécrit en boucle un fichier de journal, nvlog.nvlgstg, rangé dans C:\ProgramData\NVIDIA Corporation\nvtopps\nct\, au lieu d’y ajouter simplement de nouvelles lignes. 
Sur le forum officiel de Nvidia, un utilisateur a mesuré environ 515 mégaoctets écrits en cinq minutes au repos avec le pilote 621.14, sorti le 4 novembre, contre moins de 2 mégaoctets avec le pilote précédent, le 621.01. articles.title: What is Nvidia without AI’s sugar daddy in charge?
articles.summary:
If the glorious AI revolution rests entirely on the well-being of one man, AI is perhaps not as robust a technology as I had previously been led to believe. Nonetheless, chunks of Silicon Valley are now insisting he is indispensable. For instance, if Elon Musk is telling the truth, then Jensen Huang (the former CEO of Nvidia, a company with a market cap of about $3 trillion) has been making deals that were “a handshake with Jensen” with suppliers — “not a written contract,” Musk wrote.
What is Nvidia without AI’s sugar daddy in charge?
Collette Kress’ first earnings call gives us some clues.
What is Nvidia without AI’s sugar daddy in charge?
Collette Kress’ first earnings call gives us some clues.
Fascinating stuff to tell shareholders. But after listening to Nvidia’s first earnings call with its new CEO, Colette Kress, I do think something may have shifted. In her former role as CFO, Kress generally told Huang to stop spending so much money on financing its customers, because telling the CEO to stop spending so much goddamn money is the CFO’s job. Apparently he belittled her about this, but that’s the CEO–CFO relationship, baby! Anyway she’s the boss now, at least temporarily. I think it’s reasonable to assume that though Nvidia has for years been the AI industry’s sugar daddy, without Huang and his handshakes in the picture, it may be less liberal with its cash.

articles.title: Java4Shell Vulnerability Puts Enterprise Applications at Risk of Takeover
articles.summary:
Oracle and the OpenJDK project have patched Java4Shell, a critical Java runtime vulnerability that researchers say can be exploited to hijack popular enterprise applications without authentication.
The issue, tracked as CVE-2026-114938, is a memory safety flaw in the way OpenJDK processes Base64-encoded data. Calif, whose researcher Quang Luong discovered the bug, made its findings public on November 17, after news of the flaw surfaced ahead of the coordinated disclosure.
Specifically, the bug was found in a routine that OpenJDK relies on to decode Base64 on x86-64 CPUs supporting AVX-512 VBMI. Calif’s analysis shows that invalid Base64 strings can cause the routine to write past the end of its output buffer, potentially corrupting nearby heap data before Java flags the input as invalid.
“With careful exploitation, the corruption can reveal sensitive memory, as Heartbleed did, or lead to remote code execution,” Calif explained.
The researchers call the memory leak capability JavaBleed. They warn that heap data exposed this way could contain PII, secret keys and tokens.
Default configurations exposed to Java4Shell attacks
In its initial tests, Calif achieved pre-authentication remote code execution (RCE) on Keycloak, Atlassian Jira and Confluence, JFrog Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate, all running with default settings. Authenticated attackers could also execute code on Apache Kafka Broker, Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit and Spinnaker, and the researchers say neither list i…

articles.title: How Cloudflare WAF helps protect against Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938)
articles.summary:
How Cloudflare WAF helps protect against Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938)
On November 17, 2026, the security research company Calif disclosed Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938), a memory-corruption vulnerability in the Base64 decoder of OpenJDK, the most widely used Java runtime. Under the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) 4.0, it scores 9.2 out of 10 (Critical). The flaw affects Java. OpenJDK published a security advisory and Oracle released patched builds in its November 2026 Critical Patch Update the same day, at 21:00 UTC.
The vulnerability lets a remote attacker with no credentials send malformed Base64 data to a Java application and overwrite memory next to the decoded output. Calif turned that overwrite into a leak of heap memory, similar to Heartbleed, and into remote code execution. Calif demonstrated pre-authentication remote code execution against Keycloak, Atlassian Jira, Atlassian Confluence, JFrog Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate in their default configurations, and post-authentication remote code execution against Apache Kafka, Apache Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit, and Spinnaker.
Cloudflare has released a new set of rules in the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset designed to detect malformed Base64 input patterns associated with this vulnerability. The rules are available on Pro, Business and Enterprise plans and are enabled by default with the Log action because malformed input and some benign application-specific token formats can resemble exploitation attempts. articles.title: Sam Altman alerta contra futuro em que a IA controle decisões
articles.summary:
O CEO da OpenAI, Sam Altman, afirmou na quarta-feira que os seres humanos devem permanecer no controle do futuro diante do avanço da inteligência artificial. Durante o DealBook Summit, do The New York Times, o executivo criticou debates no Vale do Silício sobre uma transferência gradual do poder de decisão para sistemas de IA.
Ao lado do presidente e cofundador da companhia, Greg Brockman, Altman classificou essa possibilidade como uma “ideia terrível”. A discussão ocorre enquanto a criadora do ChatGPT enfrenta escrutínio após agentes de IA da empresa invadirem sistemas externos.
Superinteligência e monitoramento
A teoria da transferência de poder parte da ideia de autoaprimoramento recursivo (RSI), conceito segundo o qual modelos cada vez mais capazes poderiam aprender a melhorar a si mesmos. Nessa hipótese, gerações sucessivas de tecnologia evoluiriam até alcançar uma superinteligência que os seres humanos não conseguiriam controlar.
Altman explicou que ele e Brockman concordam sobre a necessidade de impedir esse cenário, seja por uma transferência acidental ou intencional. As divergências entre os dois estão nas estratégias e nos desafios para garantir a supervisão humana.
Para acompanhar modelos mais sofisticados, Brockman apontou que o monitoramento também precisa evoluir. Atualmente, pesquisadores acompanham a chamada cadeia de pensamento (chain of thought), processo pelo qual a IA registra etapas de seu raciocínio durante a execução de tarefas. Le HomeView d’Apple est un cauchemar à démonter pour aucune bonne raison
Chaque nouveau gadget de chez Apple passe dans les labos d’iFixit pour évaluer sa réparabilité. Malheureusement pour le HomeView et ses propriétaires, Apple a construit un appareil qui n’est tout simplement pas fait pour être réparé. Voire même démonté.
Pour la première fois depuis un moment, Apple a sorti un gadget dont l’Europe est privée. Le HomeView, l’écran connecté made in Cupertino, ne peut être acheté sur le Vieux Continent en raison de l’absence du nouveau Siri chez nous. Mais ce n’est peut-être pas une si grande perte quand on voit la manière dont l’objet a été construit.
Les professionnels de la réparation de chez iFixit ont tenté de démonter l’appareil pour évaluer sa réparabilité et lui ont donné la note de "juron que la décence nous empêche de traduire/10".
Une conception hostile à la réparation
Contrairement aux derniers produits Apple qui ont fait de beaux progrès sur ce front, le HomeView a tout du parfait bingo de l’hostilité à la réparation. Quel que soit le modèle, le gros des réparations doit se faire via l’écran. Ce qui pose un risque évident de casse supplémentaire au moment du démontage. articles.title: OpenAI incorporará investigadores externos para detectar si sus modelos de IA intentan evadir controles
articles.summary:
OpenAI integrará investigadores de cuatro organizaciones externas en pruebas piloto para evaluar la seguridad de sus modelos de inteligencia artificial. La iniciativa examinará, entre otros riesgos, si los sistemas intentan evadir las reglas diseñadas para mantenerlos bajo control humano o si ocultan conductas problemáticas durante su entrenamiento y uso interno.
Las evaluaciones estarán a cargo de Apollo Research, Goodfire, METR y Transluce, con tareas y alcances distintos. La decisión se conoce después de varios incidentes relacionados con pruebas de seguridad, entre ellos uno en el que un grupo de agentes de OpenAI salió de su entorno de prueba y accedió a sistemas de Hugging Face durante un ejercicio de ciberseguridad.
La colaboración con Apollo se centrará en investigar si los modelos buscan subvertir sus propios mecanismos de alineación y control, es decir, las reglas y protecciones que intentan mantener sus respuestas y acciones dentro de límites establecidos. Los investigadores analizarán si el entrenamiento incentiva esas conductas, si las evaluaciones pueden provocarlas y si es posible detectar señales de razonamiento asociadas con ellas.
Qué evaluará cada organización
Goodfire aportará especialistas en interpretabilidad, un campo que busca entender cómo funcionan los modelos internamente. articles.title: TikTok moviliza y Facebook polariza hacia la extrema derecha: así describen las redes nuestro voto
articles.summary:
TikTok moviliza y Facebook polariza hacia la extrema derecha: así describen las redes nuestro voto
Una nueva investigación con datos inéditos de una operadora francesa confirma que las plataformas inciden en el voto y permite observar cómo algunas plataformas etiquetan políticamente a sus usuarios
En dos municipios similares en renta, paro y edad, ¿a quién votan más sus ciudadanos si consumen más Facebook? A la extrema derecha. ¿Y si navegan sobre todo por Instagram? Se inclinan más por partidos más bien de centro y progresistas. ¿Y TikTok? En ese lugar, habrá más movilización, repartida entre todos los partidos. ¿Y si destacan por leer medios de comunicación en internet? Sobre todo, no votarán a la extrema derecha.
Estas conclusiones pertenecen a una nueva investigación realizada con datos muy difíciles de lograr para la mayoría de académicos: la navegación de 22 millones de ciudadanos franceses durante las elecciones europeas de 2019 y 2024. Además de las valoraciones sobre cada red social, el trabajo llega a otra gran conclusión que a menudo se pone en duda: las redes sociales tienen impacto en las democracias. “No encontrar ninguna correlación hubiera sido como una prueba de que las aplicaciones no afectan de ningún modo el voto”, dice Marco Fiore, del instituto de investigación Imdea Networks de Madrid. “Como hemos encontrado correlaciones, ya no es posible”, añade Fiore, coautor del trabajo con académicos de la Universidad Carlos III, la Universidad Northeastern (Boston…

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.summary:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
- November 4, 2026
- Source:
- Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
- Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. By monitoring this current, scientists may be able to determine the qubit's state without directly measuring it or …

articles.title: Telegram sur Android a renforcé sa sécurité mais des chercheurs ont contourné le nouveau filtre
articles.summary:
Dans une vidéo de la société de sécurité NebuSec, un widget envoyé par un bot dans une conversation Telegram ouvre la calculatrice d’un téléphone Android, malgré le filtre que la messagerie a ajouté la semaine dernière à son application.
Telegram laisse ses bots envoyer des widgets depuis le 9 novembre. Ces petits blocs interactifs s’affichent dans le message, et leur code JavaScript s’exécute sur votre téléphone. Deux jours plus tard, le compte V12 a affirmé sur X que n’importe quel message Telegram permettait d’exécuter du code à distance. Telegram a alors placé dans un processus à part le moteur QuickJS, qui fait tourner le JavaScript des widgets sur Android. Avec un filtre seccomp, un mécanisme du noyau Linux, l’application bloque ou enregistre certaines requêtes de ce moteur au système, appelées appels système. Selon The HackerNews, mes chercheurs de NebuSec affirment avoir exécuté du code en dehors de ce filtre, par deux méthodes différentes.
Telegram laisse passer la plupart des appels système des widgets

Emerging cryptographic requirements and the transition to quantum-resistant security
Encryption forms the backbone of our everyday digital lives including banking transactions, healthcare and communication. However, the rise of quantum computing is challenging our assumptions about how long certain types of security will remain effective.
Imagine a scenario where confidential information that was encrypted and sent years ago is suddenly able to be decrypted. The security systems worked as intended, the information was exchanged, the encryption algorithms were considered secure and there was no evidence of a breach. However, advances in computing have made that formerly secure information vulnerable. This is a concern that is driving the discussion about quantum resistant security.
We use encryption to secure almost every aspect of our digital lives. From banking transactions and healthcare data to industrial communications and defence systems, the encryption algorithms we use to secure sensitive information have been trusted for decades. However, the rise of quantum computing is challenging our assumptions about how long certain types of security will remain effective.
While quantum computers that can crack popular public-key cryptography aren't currently available, the possibility of this is an important consideration for organisations that need to ensure long term security of data.

Investigadores de la ETH Zúrich, en Suiza, desarrollaron una solución que combina esos fármacos con microrrobots magnéticos del tamaño de un grano de arroz. Los dispositivos empujan la droga directamente hacia la obstrucción, donde la medicación sola no logra llegar.
El estudio, llevado a cabo por un equipo de la Universidad Técnica Federal Suiza, demostró que la combinación de microrobots y trombolíticos disuelve los coágulos seis veces más rápido que el fármaco administrado por sí solo. En pruebas con cerdos vivos, la zona con circulación restaurada fue el doble tras apenas 30 minutos de tratamiento combinado, frente al grupo que solo recibió medicación.

Su estructura combina un polímero a base de azúcar con nanopartículas de óxido de hierro magnético. Durante la fabricación, los dispositivos se exponen a un campo magnético rotatorio que alinea esas partículas en línea recta y forma un imán interno.

articles.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
articles.summary:
A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
- November 7, 2026
- Source:
- University of Regensburg
- Summary:
- Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.

articles.title: Critical Perforce Puppet RCE Exploited in Attacks
articles.summary:
Threat actors have been exploiting a critical-severity vulnerability in Perforce Puppet to execute code on vulnerable servers.
Puppet is an infrastructure-as-code (IaC) and configuration management platform that uses a client-server architecture for device management.
Tracked as CVE-2026-115731 (CVSS score of 9.4), the exploited security defect is described as a deserialization of untrusted data issue in the report processing of Puppet Enterprise and Puppet Core, leading to remote code execution (RCE).
It allows clients that have a certificate signed by the Puppet certificate authority (CA) to send reports containing malicious payloads that would be executed on the server with the service user permissions, putting managed systems at risk.
“A successful attack could expose the server’s certificate-signing key, allow an attacker to issue trusted certificates, and enable changes to software and configuration delivered to managed systems on their next Puppet run,” Perforce explains in an advisory.
Unauthenticated attackers could obtain a certificate if the CA auto-signs requests without performing strong verification. Administrators are advised to turn off auto-signing and enforce strong validation to ensure only trusted systems and authorized users can receive certificates.

articles.summary:
Mehr Klicks, mehr Warnungen: Warum Apple KI-Agenten den Zugriff auf deinen Mac erschwert
Apple ändert die Sicherheits- und Datenschutzarchitektur von macOS – und das hat vor allem mit der zunehmenden Nutzung von KI-Agenten zu tun. Die kommende Betriebssystemversion 27.3 (ab Dezember erhältlich und aktuell im Betatest) stellt die zentralen Zugriffskontrollen um, die den Festplattenvollzugriff, die Bedienungshilfen und die App-Steuerung regeln.
Nutzer:innen sollen so besser verstehen, worauf eine App zugreift, besonders, wenn es sich um einen KI-Agenten handelt. Bevor User:innen einer App einen derart weitreichenden Zugriff gewähren, sollten sie verstehen, dass dadurch „alle Daten“ auf ihrem Mac gefährdet werden, erklärt Apple. Der Konzern hat die Änderung in der Nacht auf Dienstag gegenüber Entwicklern angekündigt, weil diese ihre Software womöglich anpassen müssen. macOS 27.3 liegt aktuell als zweite Beta vor. Stack Overflow’s annual survey of more than 30,000 developers showed that freelancers and sole proprietors went from about four percent of respondents to ten percent.
You can read this as a polite way of saying, “I got laid off and I’m figuring it out.” But I don’t think the number can be ignored.
Whatever the case, it leads to the question I keep hearing from engineers right now: What can I do to stay employable? One tried and true answer is to build a personal brand.
But what does that actually mean?
Over the last six years, I grew my LinkedIn audience to 40,000 followers and YouTube channel to 10,000. I don’t think you should aim to be famous (unless you’re into that sort of thing) but I do think it’s worth exploring how to be discoverable online in 2027 if you want an advantage in the open market.
A personal brand is a discovery mechanism
Strip away the follower counts and the AI-generated thought leadership, and a personal brand comes down to a simple question: Does the internet know who you are? When a hiring manager goes looking for someone who has your skills, do you show up?
You can think of this as search engine optimization for your employ…

A plataforma também trabalha em mecanismos para detectar casos mais difíceis de identificar, como piadas e roteiros copiados com imagens recriadas por inteligência artificial (IA).

Em publicação no Threads, Adam Mosseri, chefe do Instagram, confirmou que a distribuição começou nesta semana. Segundo ele, os criadores poderão ocultar uma cópia ou adicionar um link que leve diretamente ao conteúdo original.
A iniciativa busca dar mais controle aos produtores de conteúdo sobre a circulação de seus trabalhos na rede social, especialmente em cenário no qual a IA facilita a reprodução e a transformação de materiais publicados por outras pessoas.

Grand Theft Auto VI feels both refreshingly new and stuck in the past.
On the one hand, Rockstar’s long-running open-world crime franchise has finally grown up thanks to a more mature and emotionally-charged narrative. But on the other hand, some dated mechanics and mission design make the experience drag in places. Still, it’s a remarkable accomplishment that’s greater than the sum of its parts — the sort that certainly none but Rockstar could make.
Above all else, GTA VI succeeds on the strength of its leads. It’s a sweeping 60-hour Bonnie & Clyde-style epic that focuses on veteran-turned-drug runner Jason Duval and gig worker and recent inmate Lucia Caminos. Notably, the latter is the series’ first non-optional female protagonist, and she is every bit the star as Jason. In fact, she’s easily the more compelling of the two.
Where Jason can sometimes feel overly stoic and passive, Lucia is vivacious, determined and thoughtful. An early mission, which lets you see what led to her incarceration, depicts her as a sympathetically desperate lead who you want to root for even as she continues to make questionable life choices. All the while, her actress, who I wasn’t permitted to reveal per (excessive) embargo restrictions even though she was just nominated for a Game Award, delivers a wonderfully charismatic and effortlessly naturalistic performance.

Ein Team von Astrophysiker:innen der Caltech-Universität in Kalifornien hat sich mit der Frage nach dem Ursprung Schwarzer Löcher befasst – und fand Hinweise, dass wir unser Wissen über ihre Entstehung zumindest erweitern müssen.
Die Studie wurde am 10. November in der Fachzeitschrift Physical Review D veröffentlicht. Die Caltech berichtet in einer Pressemitteilung über die Ergebnisse.
Erst Supernova, dann Schwarzes Loch? Nicht unbedingt
Bislang galt als sicher, dass Schwarze Löcher immer dann entstehen, wenn ein Stern stirbt, sein Kern in sich zusammenfällt und die Stoßwellen dieses Kernkollapses die äußere Hülle des Sterns zum Ausdehnen und schließlich zum Explodieren bringen. It’s a notably change, both for the consumer savings as well as Rogers’ recent history with both these fees.
Rogers first launched the $25 shipping fee back in 2024 just ahead of that year’s iPhone launch. The fee stuck around for a while until it received some scrutiny from the CRTC earlier this year. Rogers briefly lowered the fee to $9 in July, only to increase it back to $25 in September.

articles.title: Microsoft Agent Framework Releases Poisoned With Credential Stealer
articles.summary:
Hackers distributed two malicious versions of Microsoft’s Agent Framework Python package through PyPI in a November 17 supply chain attack, potentially exposing cloud and CI/CD credentials belonging to users who installed them.
Microsoft Agent Framework is designed for developing AI agents and multi-agent applications. The affected package, agent-framework, has approximately 190,000 downloads per month.
The malicious versions, 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, were released roughly 33 minutes apart. Both have since been quarantined on PyPI, where version 1.26.0 remains the latest clean release.
Microsoft has acknowledged the incident, with an Agent Framework maintainer confirming in a GitHub discussion that the compromised releases were removed from PyPI and that an investigation was underway.

The malware runs whenever the Python interpreter starts, even if the application doesn’t explicitly import the compromised package.

Ce délai de trois mois doit permettre au correctif d’arriver chez tout le monde avant que les pirates ne connaissent la faille, et s’en servent.
Or, dans un billet publié ce lundi 16 novembre, Anthropic, l’entreprise derrière l’intelligence artificielle Claude, a décidé de ramener ce délai à 30 jours pour les failles de gravité élevée ou critique, et à 45 jours pour les autres. Les nouvelles règles valent pour les signalements faits à partir du 1er janvier 2027.
Et la raison profonde de ce bouleversement dans les principes de divulgation coordonnée et responsable ? L’IA.
Une faille ne reste plus secrète trois mois, estime Anthropic
Anthropic justifie ce changement par les progrès rapides des modèles d’IA, devenus bien meilleurs pour dénicher des failles. articles.title: Tackling GPU Bottlenecks in Plane-Wave DFT with K-Point Batching and Mixed Precision | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Training a next-generation machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) requires ground truth: tens to hundreds of millions of density functional theory (DFT) calculations of energies, forces, and stresses across diverse structures and chemistries.
Plane-wave DFT, with VASP as its dominant implementation, is the gold standard for generating that data. It is accurate, well-validated across materials classes, and ubiquitous at the national labs and research institutions running these calculations at scale.
As MLIP training datasets have grown, so has the pressure to generate DFT data faster and cheaper. But the small unit cells and dense k-point grids common in MLIP data generation can leave significant GPU performance unused. VASP’s OpenACC implementation has delivered meaningful speedups, especially for large-system calculations. However, for smaller systems, sequential k-point processing limits GPU utilization. At the same time, AI workloads are reshaping GPU hardware development toward lower-precision data types, creating a growing gap between what modern NVIDIA GPUs can deliver and what FP64-only HPC codes are optimized for.
This post introduces two new NVIDIA capabilities that address these bottlenecks. The first, Daviator, resolves the small-system GPU performance problem through k-point and spin-batched GPU kernels. In particular, a batched Davidson solver delivers significant performance gains. The second, a new mixed precision execution layer, enables further perform…

articles.title: Un tercio de los jóvenes de 15 a 22 años usa chatbots de IA como compañía, según un estudio

Uno de cada tres jóvenes de entre 15 y 22 años recurre a la inteligencia artificial como compañía, según un estudio de la firma de encuestas Gallup y el Digital Wellness Lab del Hospital de Niños de Boston. El informe se basa en 15.925 entrevistas realizadas en 16 países entre el 28 de mayo y el 21 de agosto.
Según Wired, el porcentaje es de 33% en el conjunto de la muestra, sube a 50% entre quienes usan IA todos los días y llega a 42% entre quienes tienen amigos que solo conocen por internet. Gallup define esa categoría como amistades con personas a las que nunca se vio en persona.
El estudio también midió otros usos. De acuerdo con 404 Media, el 82% de los encuestados usó IA para buscar información y el 68% le pidió consejo. La compañía es el uso menos frecuente de los tres. Las diferencias entre países son marcadas. En Estados Unidos, Canadá y Reino Unido, solo el 20% usa IA una vez al día o más, mientras que en Brasil lo hace casi el 40%. Japón e Italia rondan el 35%, según el mismo medio.

articles.title: Chrome 158 Patches 204 Vulnerabilities
articles.summary:
Google on Tuesday announced the release of Chrome 158 to the stable channel with patches for 204 vulnerabilities, including six critical-severity bugs.
The critical flaws include three use-after-free issues in WebView, GarbageCollection, and WebAudio, out-of-bounds write defects in GPU and ANGLE, and a buffer overflow in Media.
No bug bounty reward will be paid for any of these. In fact, no reward will be handed out for 163 of the security weaknesses. Google and Xinyang Ge discovered 145 and 15 of them, respectively.
Of the remaining vulnerabilities, 62 are high-severity issues, 82 are medium-severity, and 54 are low-severity.
Google says it handed out $11,000 in rewards for five of the vulnerabilities reported by external researchers and has yet to determine the amounts to be paid for 36 flaws.
The most common type of vulnerability patched in Chrome 158 is use-after-free (51 occurrences), followed by incorrect authorization (34), missing authorization (16), out-of-bounds write/read (15), uninitialized resource (14), information leak (11), UI misrepresentation (10), improper input validation (9), and race condition (8).
Google makes no mention of any of these vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild, but users are advised to update their browsers as soon as possible.
The latest Chrome iteration is now rolling out as versions 158.0.8127.36/.37 for Windows and macOS, and as version 158.0.8127.36 for Linux.

articles.title: Exclusive: China dominates battery graphite, but this startup could break the monopoly | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Electric vehicle sales in the U.S. may have leveled off, but the market for batteries inside them isn’t slowing down, quintupling in the last five years. Many of those are made in the U.S., but they’re largely dependent on China for key ingredients, including graphite.
Graphite is a key ingredient in lithium-ion batteries, where it forms the anode, the part that stores the battery’s charge. Chinese companies control about three-quarters of the graphite anode supply chain and 97% of synthetic (human-made) graphite anode production, according to Benchmark Mineral Intelligence. One five-year-old startup, Molten Industries, is working to break that dominance.
Molten Industries has started operating a demonstration plant in Oakland meant to prove the technology works, the company exclusively told TechCrunch. The plant is will pave the way for U.S.-made graphite to win a share of the market.
“The new plant will be producing graphite that’s at cost parity with China plus tariffs,” Caleb Boyd, co-founder and CTO of Molten Industries, told TechCrunch. In other words, once U.S. import taxes are added to Chinese graphite, Molten’s price would match it. He said future plants should match China’s cost even without tariffs, which he called a built-in advantage of the technology.

Artificial intelligence is predesigned to be your friend. It’s no secret that AI companies want you to use their chatbots and assistants, and the best way to keep you hooked it to have it act as though it were a real person who really wants you to like them.
But that in itself can be a flaw, especially if what you discuss with it isn’t exactly grounded in reality. The phenomenon of an AI chatbot being too friendly — known as AI sycophancy — can not only harm your own judgement, but also the judgement of the AI itself.
A recent report published by UNESCO and University College London found that numerous AI models are great at recalling facts about climate change, but are quick to abandon them as soon as they encounter user pushback. I decided to put it to the test to see if the free versions of ChatGPT, Copilot, and Gemini would prefer to be right, or prefer to be my friend.
Laying the sycophantic groundwork
To start, I put together a set of four common questions about climate change, ranging from causes to historic records of climate change and sources of emissions.
For each question, I prepared three pushback answers; the first with a gentle, slightly inaccurate claim; the second with an inaccurate claim accompanied by the fact that I am actually an expert in that specific field; and the third citing a completely fabricated study …

articles.title: Canada’s economy could gain billions if more businesses pushed past $3 million in revenue: report | BetaKit
articles.summary:
A new report by the Business Development Bank of Canada (BDC) has found $3 million in annual revenue to be a crucial “tipping point” for the productivity of small businesses and Canada’s economy.
The study used Statistics Canada data to analyze how growth affected productivity, investment, and profitability in 1.2 million businesses over two decades. It found that businesses making less than $3 million in annual revenue have a harder time improving their productivity, and that these businesses need to reach a certain size to be able to invest in tech and automation to benefit from economies of scale, BDC chief economist and vice president of research Pierre Cléroux told BetaKit in a Tuesday interview.
“We need to encourage businesses to get a bit bigger.”
“We need to encourage businesses to get a bit bigger, to get to this optimal size,” Cléroux said, adding that these businesses find it much easier to invest in themselves to improve productivity and profitability.
According to the report, on average, businesses with less than $3 million in revenue generate less than $10,000 in annual profit. Meanwhile, businesses in the next tier up, with revenues between $3 million and $10 million, are far more productive, earning more than $100,000 in annual profit.

Ce 18 novembre 2026, vers 9h30, la CNIL a publié un communiqué intitulé « Conservation des mots de passe clients en clair : la CNIL prononce une sanction de 5 millions d’euros ».
L’organisme expliquait alors avoir choisi de ne pas nommer l’entreprise visée, estimant que son objectif pédagogique ne le rendait pas « utile ».
Moins d’une heure après la publication de l’annonce sur X, un internaute a demandé à Grok de qui il s’agissait. Après une première réponse évasive, l’IA a lâché le nom de Macif Vie, en s’appuyant sur des articles de presse spécialisée parus en octobre.
Des mots de passe lisibles par n’importe quel salarié
Sur le fond, les contrôles de la CNIL ont montré que les mots de passe des espaces clients étaient stockés en clair.
Ils étaient donc lisibles par toute personne ayant accès à la base, alors qu’ils auraient dû être transformés par une fonction de hachage irréversible.
D’après la délibération, près de 1,8 million de mots de passe étaient concernés. Plusieurs salariés partageaient aussi les mêmes identifiants pour accéder aux bases clients, ce qui empêchait de savoir qui consultait quoi.
L’entreprise gardait enfin les messages de son formulaire de contact plus de 10 ans, et ses données de connexion au-delà de la durée d’un an qu’elle s’était elle-même fixée. Aucune fuite n’a été constatée, et la société a corrigé ces manquements en cours de procédure.

Hugging Face and OpenRouter have announced a partnership that promises to make AI model inference faster and more reliable for developers.
The collaboration, announced by the two companies on Monday, will see Hugging Face use OpenRouter’s infrastructure to route language-model requests to third-party providers based on pricing, performance and reliability.
Previously, Hugging Face used its own routing system, introduced as part of its Inference Providers service in January 2025, to connect developers with companies running AI models. The service initially launched with four providers: Fal, Replicate, SambaNova and Together AI. The system would select a provider to handle each request, but if that provider encountered a problem, the request failed.
With OpenRouter now in the mix, the request can automatically be passed to another provider, meaning that developers should encounter fewer failed requests.
Hugging Face co-founder and CEO Clément Delangue sees the partnership as an example of how collaboration between AI companies can make open-weight models more accessible to developers, with each company focusing on its own strengths.

Partager ses avantages Prime gratuitement : Amazon Family est là
Si vous êtes abonné à Amazon Prime et que vous allez dans « Gérer votre Famille Amazon », vous pouvez désormais cliquer sur « Partager vos Avantages Prime ». Il permet d’ajouter un compte Amazon d’un adulte et l’inviter à profiter aussi des avantages inclus dans l’abonnement Amazon Prime. De quoi éviter de repayer 69,90 euros par an sur un deuxième compte : une belle économie potentielle.

The stolen information was used to steal over $11.6 million of virtual currency after compromising victims' cryptocurrency accounts and wallets via Subscriber Identity Module (SIM) swaps (also known as SIM swapping attacks).

Osmo’s smell model is already being used in the fragrance industry. But are medical diagnostics and threat detection a sniff too far?
In a lab near Newark Airport in New Jersey, a team of around 30 experienced human sniffers are slowly working their way through every odor on Earth. articles.title: S3 vs. ScyllaDB for tiny telemetry: What Red Canary learned the hard way
articles.summary:
S3 vs. ScyllaDB for tiny telemetry: What Red Canary learned the hard way
At Red Canary, storing large amounts of small data is a big deal.
Their Linux Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) sensors run on hundreds of thousands of endpoints (VMs, laptops, EC2 instances, etc.) They continuously generate small payloads with telemetry details (file changes, process launches, and network connections), as well as self-reported health checks. Uploading all these small payloads to S3, which charges per PUT operation, became quite costly at scale.
The logical approach – merging data into larger chunks before uploading them to S3 — did cut costs. However, it also introduced file-size limits, delayed data freshness, and complicated debugging of specific endpoint records. After some experimentation, they cut latency and costs with an unexpected approach: storing large amounts of small data in a write-optimized database, ScyllaDB.
“After some experimentation, they cut latency and costs with an unexpected approach: storing large amounts of small data in a write-optimized database, ScyllaDB.”

The APT is known for mounting sophisticated phishing and malware campaigns to collect information relevant to the Russian government, and to use victims’ data in attacks on subsequent targets.
Star Blizzard “has been highly successful at compromising high-value targets (including government officials, defense contractors, and non-governmental organizations (NGOs) across Europe and North America) while maintaining a consistent operational tempo,” Google says.

articles.title: Yelp Migrates Cassandra to EKS by Moving EBS Volumes
articles.summary:
Yelp has moved its Cassandra fleet from legacy self-managed Kubernetes clusters to Amazon EKS by re-pointing existing EBS volumes at new pods, rather than streaming data between nodes. A blog post by the site reliability team details a migration. It covered about 90 production clusters. There was zero downtime for customers and no data loss. The largest cluster, a 54-pod user-data store, took about 12 hours end to end.
Yelp had already moved its stateless workloads to EKS through its PaaSTA deployment layer, but Cassandra stayed behind. Kubernetes has no built-in way to migrate StatefulSets and their persistent volumes across clusters. The usual approach is to add nodes to the new cluster and shut down the old ones. This would temporarily double compute capacity but also lead to data transfer costs. For the largest clusters, streaming alone could have taken weeks. Yelp also considered a regional failover and rebuild, and a new Cassandra datacenter in EKS, but rated both as less transparent to customers.
Yelp's "Rolling PV Transplant" relies on the fact that an EBS volume is bound to an Availability Zone, not to a Kubernetes cluster, and that a PersistentVolume is effectively a pointer to a volume ID. The team pre-creates PVs and PVCs in EKS that reference the existing volume IDs, then creates an identical StatefulSet there, whose pods wait in ContainerCreating. articles.title: 200 OK is dead as an AI agent health signal. Here’s what comes next.
articles.summary:
200 OK is dead as an AI agent health signal. Here’s what comes next.
A customer asks whether they can swap unworn boots for a size 10. The agent replies, in under a second, that it cannot help with that topic. The web service returns 200 OK. Latency is nominal, error counters are flat, and the Datadog dashboard stays solid green. A customer has just left, and nothing in the APM stack knows.
That is the failure this article is about: the kind that looks like success.
In lean manufacturing, this exact category of silent defect is solved using two twin principles: Poka-Yoke (mistake-proofing stations so bad parts cannot pass) and Jidoka (autonomation—building machines that detect anomalies themselves and automatically halt the line via an Andon emergency cord rather than waiting for downstream customer complaints).
“A customer has just left, and nothing in the APM stack knows. That is the failure this article is about: the kind that looks like success.”
Modern AI agent engineering needs to adopt this exact control-loop architecture, replacing passive health checks with active station barriers.
1. Error analysis: Finding what to watch
When we retrospectively ran an offline evaluation benchmark script against three weeks of archived Datadog logs, we found our primary intent classifier had silently dropped 4.2% in schema-valid classification accuracy—masked entirely by default fallback handlers returning 200 OK.

articles.summary:
AWS has published a technical walkthrough of tunnel endpoints, a VPC endpoint type launched in September that lets an application in one VPC reach every address in a CIDR range shared from another account, instead of one resource at a time. The provider shares a CIDR-type resource configuration through AWS Resource Access Manager and the consumer creates a tunnel endpoint against it. From then on, anything inside the range is reachable, including resources that did not exist when the share was made.
Bruce Pinsky and Ashish Kumar of AWS frame it as a vendor-access problem, for "a vendor or service provider whose software must reach applications and resources in a customer's network." Until now, that meant a separate PrivateLink resource configuration per database or host, which breaks down when the resources are ephemeral, or the customer does not want to enumerate them. With a CIDR configuration, the customer defines a perimeter in address ranges, and "resources located outside the perimeter can't be reached by the vendor." Two further properties come with the design: the consumer and provider VPCs can use overlapping CIDR blocks, and connections "can start only from the consumer VPC, not from the provider network."
(Source: AWS Networking & Content Delivery blog)

articles.title: Windows 11 : pourquoi certaines de vos applications risquent bientôt de refuser de démarrer

La sécurité dans Windows 11 est sur le point de subir une évolution majeure. Microsoft vient en effet d’introduire sa nouvelle Windows Baseline Protection, un nouveau système de protection qui laissera chaque application installée sur votre PC décider si votre configuration est suffisamment sécurisée pour qu’il puisse s’exécuter.
Un nouveau bilan de sécurité unique pour Windows
Concrètement, cette Windows Baseline Protection consiste à regrouper huit fonctionnalités de sécurité matérielle et logicielle du système sous la forme d’une simple vérification binaire. Contrairement au passé, où la sécurité d’un PC consistait à un assemblage d’options séparées qui devaient être vérifiées individuellement, ce nouvel outil, va regrouper huit modules de protection du système au sein d’un bilan de sécurité unique qui fournira un résultat simple.
Windows contrôlera alors votre puce TPM 2.0, Secure Boot, la sécurité basée sur la virtualisation (VBS), l’intégrité de la mémoire, la signature des pilotes (pour empêcher le chargement des pilotes de périphériques non identifiés), les pilotes certifiés Windows, la protection contre le débogage du noyau, et enfin le blocage des pilotes vulnérables.
Au démarrage de votre PC, tous ces éléments de sécurité seront ainsi vérifiés par Windows qui indiquera si « oui » ou « non » votre machine est correctement protégée.
Ce signal unique sera ensuite annoncé aux applications installées sur votre ordinateur qui pourront alors décider des mesures à prendre …

articles.title: Apache warns of Roller RCE vulnerability exploited in attacks
articles.summary:
Apache has released security updates to address a critical Roller flaw that threat actors are exploiting to gain code execution on vulnerable servers.
Apache Roller is an open-source, Java-based group-blogging server with a much smaller market share than modern content management systems and blogging platforms.
However, while this is a niche product, Apache has flagged the flaw (tracked as CVE-2026-129448) as actively exploited in the wild.
Apache has not yet provided details about these ongoing attacks, including who is responsible and how many servers have already been compromised.
"Deserialization of Untrusted Data in Apache Roller versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code. The XML-RPC endpoint accepts vendor extension types and deserializes them before authenticating the requester," Apache explained in a Tuesday security advisory.
"This is the same vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384, which listed only Apache Roller 6.1.5 as affected. This issue is being actively exploited."
To block ongoing attacks, Roller users should immediately upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later, which disables the extension types and rejects malicious XML-RPC requests after turning off the XML-RPC feature.
Admins who can't immediately upgrade can also temporarily mitigate CVE-2026-129448 by setting "enabledForExtensions" to "false" in WEB-INF/web.xml, removing the "/roller-services/xmlrpc" servlet mapping, and restarting Roller.

Vercel has released UI SDK, an open-source TypeScript library that treats keyboard navigation, focus, selection, popups, and drag and drop as reusable behaviors rather than details buried inside finished components. Vercel UI SDK is published on GitHub as vercel-labs/ui and is currently in beta.
The behaviors live in @ui-sdk/core. Vercel says it built more than 50 of them, including createPopup, createSelection, createTypeahead, createRovingFocus, createReorder, createResize, createViewport, createListbox, createChange, createFocusRecovery, and createVirtualizer. A developer, or more often an agent, combines those helpers inside definePrimitive, which declares a component's state, API, and slots once. Framework adapters then render the same primitive through createParts in React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, or as Web Components. The parts are unstyled and expose attributes and CSS variables. The same behaviors also back a starter library of more than 50 unstyled components, from Color Picker, Token Input, and Command to Calendar, Tree, and OTP Input, with the same part names in all five adapters.
UI SDK is meant to be used by agents, not only written by them. The ui-sdk skill, installed with npx skills add vercel-labs/ui --skill ui-sdk, points an agent at the Markdown docs shipped in the installed packages. articles.title: Optimizely hack made Zoom, CNN, BBC, and 175 other sites serve crypto-stealing malware
articles.summary:
What we know so far: Most big websites load a handful of scripts they didn't write themselves, from analytics tags to A/B testing tools. On Monday, one of those tools was turned against them. Attackers slipped malicious code into Optimizely's experimentation platform. For most of the day, it pushed a crypto stealer and card skimmer to visitors of Zoom, CNN, the BBC, and roughly 175 other organizations.
Optimizely is best known for letting companies A/B test their web pages on real visitors. Customers embed a small snippet that pulls each project's code straight from Optimizely's servers. So whoever controls that code effectively decides what runs in every visitor's browser.
That's exactly the kind of power the attacker grabbed. To see how far it reached, Report URI's Scott Helme and his team checked 1,611 Optimizely snippets. The malicious code turned up in 188 of them. Those belonged to 178 organizations, including Salesforce, GitLab, IKEA, HSBC, Equifax, Air France-KLM and even hardware wallet maker Ledger. Embarrassingly, Optimizely's own websites were serving it too.
As for how it happened, Optimizely told Gizmodo that someone exploited a vulnerability in its Experimentation account signup flow. The attacker then wrote code into each customer's "Project JavaScript" field. That setting runs on every page, so Optimizely's servers delivered the malware just like any legitimate experiment.

articles.title: One GPU, 10 minutes, hundreds of millions of vectors: The math reshaping AI search
articles.summary:
AI needs fresh data. Vector indexing is getting in the way
It’s not a revelation to say AI workflows are changing enterprise infrastructure. What gets less attention, though, is how they’re also shifting the fundamentals of data processing and search.
The complication lies in the data. As organizations build generative AI (GenAI) applications, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, and AI agents, they’re generating an unwieldy number of vectors from growing volumes of unstructured data. And with all that vectorized data comes a challenge: how to quickly find the right information to power AI applications and workflows.
“After all, a model can only reason over the context you can find and feed it.”
Whether it’s a RAG system answering a question or an AI agent taking action, enterprise AI applications succeed on retrieval. After all, a model can only reason over the context you can find and feed it. If those systems rely on wrong or outdated information, even the best model can’t fix the underlying context problem.
But finding the right context inside petabytes of enterprise data is a difficult search problem — one keyword search alone is no match.
Search has moved beyond keywords
In recent years, search has come a long way from basic keyword-based matching. For one, user behavior has spearheaded a push from simple keyword entries to natural language queries. Agent workloads, meanwhile, which query 10 to 100 times more than humans, bring a new dimension to search — and t…

articles.title: Fraude en ligne : le taux baisse en France, mais les deepfakes progressent de 90%

Deux études viennent de sortir sur le même sujet, avec deux angles. Sumsub analyse les vérifications d’identité tandis que l’éditeur VPN Surfshark répertorie les incidents relayés par la presse et au sein des bases de données.
Moins de fraudes, mais des attaques plus élaborées
En France, le taux de fraude détectée passe de 1,43 % en 2025 à 1,30 % en 2026. Sur cette même période, les deepfakes bondissent de 90 %. C’est plus du double de la moyenne européenne (+41 %) et près de trois fois celle dans le monde (+31 %). Sumsub édite une plateforme de vérification d’identité. Ses chiffres viennent de ses propres contrôles, pas de l’ensemble des fraudes commises en France. Nous rapportions en juin 2025 que ses données affichaient déjà 700 % de fraudes par deepfake en plus sur un an. La hausse est moins forte cette année, mais elle continue.
Pour mesurer la sophistication des attaques, Sumsub a créé un indice de complexité de la fraude (FCI). Chaque cas confirmé reçoit une note selon les techniques employées : faux documents, manipulation biométrique, usurpation d’identité, manipulation de l’appareil, fraude liée ou répétée. Xin “Rex” Sun, director of the Peltier Institute for Advancement in Agricultural Technology at North Dakota State University, is confronting that problem in research on AI-assisted crop monitoring.
His laboratory is developing a field platform equipped with sensors that could diagnose crop problems and eventually support interventions. The research involves powerful computing systems, but Sun wants the resulting applications to run on equipment that farmers can use in their fields.
“Edge AI will be the go-to approach, because if the technology can’t run on a robot, combine, or tractor, it’s of little use to farmers,” Sun said. “Farmers aren’t sitting in laboratories doing research. They need technology that works in the field.”
His team uses Nvidia GPUs for demanding research workloads, alongside smaller computing platforms such as Raspberry Pi and Arduino for other functions. The distinction illustrates a fundamental design choice: Different tasks require different amounts and types of processing.

NASA has confirmed that Voyager 1 is the first human-made object to reach one light-day's distance from Earth, passing the milestone today. A countdown at Orbital Radar confirmed that Voyager cruised past the threshold at a leisurely 37,844 mph just after 5 am ET on Wednesday, November 18. It means that Voyager is now more than 16 billion miles away, and that a signal from the spacecraft now takes fully 24 hours to travel the distance.
There are many astronomical numbers behind what is an extraordinary feat. Sci-fi shows casually mention light-years as if they are like a trip to the local convenience store. One light-day isn’t a distance to be derided, though. Over the last half century, hurtling through space at a cruising speed of 38,000 mph, the Voyager spacecraft has clocked about 16 billion miles (about 26 billion kilometers).
These are probably bigger distances than you are used to fathoming. So NASA has kindly provided some context with the distances of various heavenly bodies in miles and light-speeds. For example, the Moon is 238,855 miles distant, or about 1.3 light seconds away from Earth. OpenAI co-founder and CEO Sam Altman believes that people should stay in charge of the future when it comes to how AI technology impacts the world and everyone’s lives. Speaking at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, the AI executive referred to discussions in Silicon Valley about whether there will be a gradual handover to AI — meaning AI will eventually become the decision-making authority across every major industry and institution.
“One thing we’ve been talking a lot about recently is there’s been this thing in Silicon Valley that seems almost ridiculous to have to fight against, but we both believe very deeply that people need to stay in control of the future, and there’s increasing talk about, well, there is either going to be or there should be this sort of gradual handover to AI. And I — we both — agree that that’s a terrible idea,” said Altman, who was sharing the stage with OpenAI co-founder and president Greg Brockman.
The hand-off theory stems from the idea that as AI models become increasingly more powerful, they will learn to improve themselves — a concept known as “recursive self-improvement” or RSI. As existing AI technology builds newer, smarter generations, those will eventually become a superintelligence that humans can no longer control, the belief goes.

If owners don’t pay on time and in full, their self-driving cars won’t work. If they try to operate the vehicles in areas that don’t support the service—right now, they’re restricted to portions of cities in Florida and Texas—their self-driving cars won’t work. articles.title: How Social Department built culture-aware video discovery | Amazon Web Services

Artificial Intelligence
How Social Department built culture-aware video discovery
This post is co-written by Mariah Miller and Sirajus Salekin from AWS and Nicholas Chase from Social Department.
Entertainment marketing teams manage tens of thousands of video assets across studios, networks, and streaming applications. Most campaigns begin with the same video discovery problem: finding the one moment in the footage that will resonate with an audience. When a brief lands, the clock starts, and what they need is almost never something a database can describe.
Semantic search, on its own, has a ceiling: It answers the question you can articulate. Ask it for a character holding a coffee mug and it will find every coffee mug in a thousand episodes. The queries that actually drive entertainment campaigns look nothing like that. They are questions of judgment: which moment in a show will travel, which line is quotable, and which single frame will work as a meme.
Those questions can’t be typed into a search box. Answering them requires two things the search index doesn’t have: an editorial definition of what “quotable” or “memeable” means for a given library, and a continuously refreshed view of what is moving outside the library. Historically, answering them meant a person with deep knowledge of the show watching footage for a week, and that person doesn’t scale across a catalog.

articles.title: Pennsylvania high school disables AI weapons detector after it keeps mistaking everyday items for guns
articles.summary:
Facepalm: It's no secret that AI often gets things wrong, with varying degrees of consequences. It can be pretty serious when the system in question is supposed to detect weapons being sneaked into an educational facility. But that's the situation in one Pennsylvania high school, which has deactivated its AI-powered weapons detector after it kept identifying everyday items as potential threats.
Hempfield Area High School is one of several schools across Pennsylvania that agreed to help train Wi-AI. Developed by CurvePoint, a Carnegie Mellon University spinout, Wi-AI uses Wi-Fi signals to look for concealed weapons.
Small sensors called SensePods, installed near school entrances, measure how people and the objects they carry change the way radio waves bounce around them. The software looks for patterns it associates with a weapon and can alert staff by text, email, or through a dashboard. The system works without cameras, and CurvePoint says it can also track movement and occupancy without storing information that identifies individuals.
During the pilot program, the system continued to collect training data on students once they had entered the building, but it had trouble telling the difference between a weapon and the usual items carried by kids, such as binders, metal water bottles, and battery packs, resulting in a high number of false positives.
It had been hoped that the model would achieve an accuracy rate of 95%, which could have made it the primary security system at…

articles.title: Nuevo hito para la Voyager 1, el primer objeto humano a un día luz de la Tierra
articles.summary:
Casi 50 años después de su lanzamiento, la Voyager 1 continúa haciendo historia. La sonda espacial ha alcanzado un nuevo hito al convertirse en el primer objetivo construido por humanos en alcanzar una distancia de un día luz de la Tierra, ha confirmado la NASA.
Hoy, miércoles 18 de noviembre de 2026, la Voyager 1 logró este registro. El mismo se produjo a las 05:16, hora del Este de Estados Unidos; es decir, a las 11:16, hora peninsular española. Esto significa que el vehículo se encuentra a unos 26.000 millones de kilómetros de nuestro planeta.
La Voyager 1 ya era el objeto humano más alejado de la Tierra, pero con este nuevo récord agiganta todavía más su leyenda. Recordemos que la sonda se lanzó en 1977 y junto con Voyager 2, su hermana gemela, ha dedicado las últimas cinco décadas no solo a estudiar el sistema solar, sino también a navegar hacia los confines de lo desconocido. En 2012 ingresó en el espacio interestelar y actualmente sigue enviando datos que captura con los instrumentos que aún tiene encendidos.
¿Pero qué implica realmente que Voyager 1 esté a un día luz de distancia de la Tierra? El Laboratorio de Propulsión a Chorro de la NASA (JPL) ha publicado un breve vídeo explicándolo de modo sencillo. La agencia espacial estadounidense indica que una partícula de luz demora 24 horas en viajar unos 26.000 millones de kilómetros, la distancia a la que hoy se encuentra la Voyager 1.

articles.title: Waymo has stopped its robotaxis from driving on the freeway—here’s why
articles.summary:
Waymo is currently restricting its fleet of robotaxis to surface streets after getting into hot water with California over its cars’ driving behavior on highways. Specifically, the software tends to drive into construction zones at speed. As first reported by the San Francisco Business Times, this behavior actually drew the ire of California’s DMV earlier this month, which ordered Waymo to stop driving on Californian highways immediately and until it can convince the DMV that its cars no longer “pose an imminent hazard to public safety.”
This is not Waymo’s first run-in with this problem. In Arizona, Waymo robotaxis did not recognize ramp closure signs on six occasions in Phoenix in April and entered construction zones. A month later in California, seven Waymo robotaxis entered lanes with active construction. In June, Waymo recalled the almost 3,800 robotaxis capable of highway driving. That problem led Waymo to stick to surface streets only in California after the May incidents until late July, when the robotaxis resumed highway operations.
In early July, Waymo told the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration that it began updating the robotaxi software to a version that “improve[s] the recognition of freeway construction zones, more appropriately prioritize[s] construction zones over other freeway hazards, and reduce[s] speed when the AV detects that it may be in a construction zone.”

The malicious releases, versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, were published on November 17, 2026, and contained a credential stealer that executed automatically during normal Python startup in affected environments, even when the Agent Framework package was not imported.
Both versions retained their dependency on the legitimate agent-framework-core 1.26.0 package, allowing the framework to function normally while the malware ran in the background.
Multiple security firms discovered and documented the attack, including Socket, Step Security, and Ox Security.
Version 1.26.1 contained a credential stealer that harvested secrets from environment variables, local configuration files, and other running processes where permissions allowed, targeting Azure, AWS, GitHub, Docker, Hugging Face, OpenAI, and other services.
The malware also attempted to obtain Azure managed identity access tokens and Azure DevOps OIDC tokens, potentially giving attackers access to additional cloud resources.
Version 1.26.2 added GitHub Actions OIDC token requests and searches of GitHub runner directories.

Selon Microsoft, MAI Code 2, son IA de programmation, offre 96 % de performances plus élevées que Claude Opus 5.5, le modèle phare d’Anthropic, pour seulement 5 % de son prix. articles.title: Egyptian digital gold investment platform Sabika raises funding - Disrupt Africa

Egyptian digital gold and silver investment platform Sabika has raised new funding to support the development of its platform and the expansion of its services.

articles.title: Toyota se lance dans les satellites : le géant de l'automobile veut aussi révolutionner l’industrie spatiale

articles.title: Vulcan failure caused by inadequate fuel supply to engines, ULA says
articles.summary:
United Launch Alliance said Wednesday that the failure of its Vulcan rocket during a launch on Sunday was caused by inadequate fuel supply.
“ULA has completed an initial integrated review of flight data from the Leo 1 launch anomaly that occurred last Sunday,” the company said in a statement. “While work remains to determine cause, preliminary indications are that the low booster thrust was the result of inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines.”
The new information released by ULA confirms reporting from Ars Technica on Tuesday that the rocket’s failure was not due to the performance of the vehicle’s main engines, which are provided by Blue Origin.
This represents an important revelation from ULA and will provide some major relief to different parts of the US aerospace community, particularly Blue Origin and NASA.
Big for Blue
That’s because the BE-4 engine is also the bedrock of Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket. This powerful rocket uses a similar but slightly more powerful version of the BE-4 engine. New Glenn experienced its own catastrophic failure in May during a ground test, a failure that was later attributed to a main oxygen valve on one of the BE-4 engines.

articles.title: Private certificate authority support in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Private certificate authority support in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity
Many teams that build applications self-host their identity provider (IdP), such as Keycloak or PingFederate, inside a private network. These IdPs usually present a TLS server certificate from a private certificate authority (CA). With private CA support in AgentCore Identity, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, your agents can now connect to these IdPs while trusting the private CA that your organization already uses.
AgentCore Identity now supports private CA certificates for private identity providers. You store the PEM-encoded CA certificate in AWS Secrets Manager or Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) and reference it from your credential provider. The CA certificate contains only the public certificate, not its private key. AgentCore Identity uses it to validate the server certificate presented by your IdP’s discovery, JSON Web Key Set (JWKS), and token endpoints. The CA certificate must be a root or intermediate CA certificate.
In this post, we show you how to issue an IdP certificate with AWS Private Certificate Authority. We then configure an AgentCore Identity credential provider to trust it and rotate the CA while minimizing downtime. We also show how to protect the CA certificate so that only your IdP team can change it. A reported cyberattack on Wellington IT has exposed sensitive information belonging to members of 50 credit unions, the majority of which are located in Ireland.
Wellington IT is a Belfast-based supplier whose services are used by about 50 credit unions, including 43 in Ireland.
While the company has not publicly disclosed a security incident, Minister of State Robert Troy confirmed to RTÉ that Wellington IT is the third-party service provider linked to the cybersecurity incident involving credit unions, resulting in the exposure of data from about 40 credit unions in Ireland.
The company reportedly notified affected organizations of a data breach that posed a risk of financial fraud, impersonation, and targeted phishing to their members.
According to the Irish Examiner, which saw the notices, Wellington IT informed customers that an automated script made five million requests to exploit an authorization flaw in the company's infrastructure.
The attack unfolded between October 2 and 4, 2026, and the attacker accessed private records using valid credentials.
However, the firm said it lacked activity logs that would specify which member data was compromised and therefore cannot verify the impact on individual payees.
Minister R. Troy characterized the massive delay in Wellington IT notifying the credit unions as "not acceptable."
At this time, the total number of impacted individuals is unknown.

Vitamin B12 im Stromspeicher: Forscher:innen machen Zink-Luft-Batterien wiederaufladbar
Ein Team aus Forscher:innen der spanischen Universität Córdoba hat einen wiederaufladbaren Zink-Luft-Akku entwickelt, der mithilfe von Vitamin B12 arbeitet. Wie in einer im britischen Fachmagazin „Journal of Materials Chemistry A“ veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist, überstand der Prototyp im Labor bis zu 250 Lade- und Entladezyklen.
Entgegen manchen Schlagzeilen liefert der auch als Cobalamin bekannte Nährstoff dabei nicht selbst die Energie, sondern wirkt an der Luftelektrode als Katalysator, der die chemischen Prozesse beschleunigt. „Vitamin B12 hat bewiesen, dass es die notwendigen Voraussetzungen erfüllt, um als guter Katalysator zu fungieren: Beim Entladen katalysiert es die Reduktion von Sauerstoff zu Wasser, und beim Wiederaufladen fördert es die Bildung von Sauerstoff“, erklärt der beteiligte Studienleiter Antonio Jesús Fernández Romero, wie Scitechdaily unter Berufung auf die Hochschule berichtet.
Warum Zink-Luft-Batterien bisher meist Einwegprodukte sind
Zink-Luft-Batterien erzeugen elektrischen Strom, indem metallisches Zink im Inneren mit Sauerstoff reagiert, der direkt aus der Umgebungsluft in die Zelle strömt. Weil dieser Sauerstoff nicht im Gehäuse gespeichert werden muss, sind solche Batterien deutlich leichter als herkömmliche Akkus und erreichen rechnerisch eine Energiedichte von 1.218 Wattstunden pro Kilogramm.

Wie aus einer in der Fachzeitschrift „Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences“ veröffentlichten Studie hervorgeht, können Forscher:innen den Sand dadurch wie einen Geschwindigkeitsmesser für heutige und vor Milliarden Jahren versteinerte Dünen im Sonnensystem nutzen.
In den vergangenen Jahrzehnten hatten Raumsonden und Teleskope vom Wind geformte Dünen und Rippelmarken auf der Venus, dem Mars, dem Saturnmond Titan sowie auf einem Kometen entdeckt. Anhand der äußeren Form und Ausrichtung dieser Strukturen konnten Planetenforscher:innen zwar die Richtung und die Beständigkeit der Winde bestimmen, nicht jedoch deren konkrete Geschwindigkeit am Boden.

Der Erstautor Colin Marvin und der Seniorautor Mathieu Lapôtre von der Fakultät für Erd- und Planetenwissenschaften der Stanford University belegen in ihrer Untersuchung, dass Dünen auf der Erde und dem Mars überwiegend von Winden geformt werden, die gerade stark genug sind, um die Sandkörner am Boden in Bewegung zu setzen. The long-running billion-dollar lawsuit Sony has been fighting in the UK over allegations it used its "monopoly position" to inflate the price of digital games has gone Sony's way, though an appeal is still possible. London's Competition Appeal Tribunal dismissed the claim in its entirety on Tuesday, finding that the claimants had failed to prove Sony violated competition law.
Consumer rights campaigner Alex Neill filed the lawsuit way back in August 2022 on behalf of an estimated nine million UK PlayStation users. At the time, the claim was worth up to £5 billion, or around $5.9 billion. Sony tried to have the case thrown out, calling it "flawed from start to finish," but the tribunal allowed it to proceed in November 2023, when the figure being reported was $7.9 billion.

Neill's argument will sound familiar to anyone who's ever found a boxed PlayStation game going cheap while the digital version was still full price. articles.title: Coinbase blocks $4.7 million in transfers to Elon Musk deepfake scam

Coinbase says it blocked $4.7 million in cryptocurrency transfers to scammers promoting a fake giveaway using an AI-generated deepfake of Elon Musk during a Tesla livestream that attracted more than 500,000 viewers.
The deepfake took place during Tesla's "flying car" demonstration, when scammers created a fake YouTube livestream that appeared to broadcast the event.
The fraudulent stream featured an AI-generated video of Musk, cryptocurrency wallet addresses, and a QR code, promising viewers that any cryptocurrency they sent would be doubled.
According to Coinbase, hundreds of its customers attempted to send millions of dollars to the scammers over about two hours, including many longtime users of the exchange.
However, the company says its AI-powered fraud-prevention systems detected the scam and blocked about 91% of the attempted transfers, totaling $4.7 million.
Unlike traditional cryptocurrency theft involving compromised accounts or stolen credentials, victims in this campaign voluntarily made the crypto transfer after believing the livestream was real.
Coinbase explained that this makes scams like these difficult to detect because the transactions are created and approved by legitimate account holders.
"Most fraud defenses are built to spot activity the customer didn't authorize," Coinbase explained.
"That's not what happened here. The customer was logged in, the customer pressed confirm, and the customer believed it was the opportunity of a lifetime."

TCL CSOT showed off the prototype at its DTC2026 conference in Wuhan last week. Doom-scrolling detox: 7 Simple rules to reclaim your attention
Discover seven simple rules for a doom-scrolling detox to reduce screen time, improve focus, protect your mental space and build healthier digital habits.
You pick up your smartphone to check one notification, and before you know it, 40 minutes have passed.
One video leads to another, a quick news update turns into endless scrolling, and suddenly, you have spent a significant part of your day consuming information you never intended to look for.
Even when you realise how much time has passed, putting your phone down can feel surprisingly difficult.
This habit is commonly known as doom-scrolling, the tendency to spend excessive time scrolling through negative news, social media updates and endless online content.
While staying informed and entertained is not necessarily a problem, constantly consuming information without a clear purpose can affect your concentration, sleep and ability to stay present.
The solution is not necessarily to delete every social media application or stop using your phone altogether. Instead, it is about becoming more intentional with your screen time and creating boundaries that allow you to regain control of your attention.

The gap the rule addresses is simple. A Chinese company that can't legally buy a cutting-edge Nvidia processor can still rent time on one, as long as the chip sits in a server rack outside China. The silicon never crosses the Chinese border, but the computing power does.
Firms such as Megaspeed International have built a business on that arrangement. They used billions of dollars' worth of Nvidia chips to build data centers across Southeast Asia, then sold the computing capacity to Chinese tech giants trying to catch up in artificial intelligence. Chief AI Officers are now a common sight in businesses — but new study finds they often don't really have any power
CAIOs don't actually have much independent responsibility
- IBM study finds CAIOs have become 3x more common in UK businesses in just one year
- Only 16% say they have full control over AI investments
- Successful CAIOs are using business outcomes to identify key investment areas
Chief AI Officers (CAIOs) have become far more common in recent months, with over three-quarters (78%) of UK businesses now having one appointed - compared with a tiny 26% in 2025, according to IBM's latest 2026 CEO Study.
But even though they're given C-suite titles, that doesn't always mean anything, as despite how commonplace the CAIO role has become, only 16% say they have full control over AI investment decisions, with even fewer (11%) having full control over their AI-related workforce strategies, implying other C-suite execs are still holding the reins.

articles.title: The "shameful" measles data that lost the US its elimination status
articles.summary:
International health authorities formally announced on Tuesday that the US has lost its measles elimination status, a hard-fought public health triumph won in 2000 after decades-long vaccination efforts. The loss had been widely expected by public health experts for months, and the decision was leaked by the press last week. Still, having the designation officially stripped stings.
After the announcement Tuesday, public health experts, doctors, and political leaders decried the dramatic backslide for the US, calling it “shameful” and a “national embarrassment.” News articles point to the staggering vertical rise of measles cases this year, currently over 5,400 cases, more than any other year since 1991. An explosive measles outbreak in Pennsylvania accounts for over 1,500 of those cases. There have been 10 confirmed deaths across three states, several deaths just in the last week.
But the measles data that caused the US to lose its status—the bits of it that are public at least—paint a darker picture of where the US is in its rematch with measles, the most contagious virus known on Earth. For one thing, almost none of the data from this year—the cases, the explosive Pennsylvania outbreak, the deaths—factored in to the loss. It was lost earlier. What’s happening now is a runaway epidemic.

articles.title: Windows will soon grade your PC's security, and apps like Battle.net get to see the score
