The big picture: Plenty of online PC games already refuse to launch unless Secure Boot is enabled. Microsoft now wants to turn checks like that into one standard question that any Windows 11 app can ask your PC. If the answer comes back no, the developer decides what happens next. Some apps may just show a warning; others could refuse to run altogether.
Microsoft calls the feature Windows baseline protection. Insiders can already try it, though a broader release isn't planned until 2027. None of the protections it checks are actually new. The feature simply rolls eight existing ones into a single pass-or-fail result. Those include TPM 2.0, Secure Boot, virtualization-based security, and memory integrity, along with a few rules that stop unsigned or known-flawed drivers from loading.
Ironically, Microsoft's own advice could trip up some gamers. Back in 2022, it suggested turning off memory integrity to claw back a few frames. Windows began switching the feature on automatically in October, but PCs where someone disabled it by hand are left alone, so those machines fail the check.
Secure Boot causes the same problem for anyone who switched it off to dual-boot Linux. Those PCs already can't play Battlefield 6, since its anti-cheat demands Secure Boot too.

Starburst Data Inc. is expanding its data federation platform into business context management with the introduction of Context Studio, a new capability designed to help artificial intelligence agents produce more accurate and trustworthy answers from information distributed across enterprise systems.
Context Studio collects business definitions from existing data catalogs, business intelligence tools, metric stores and documents, making them available alongside data when AI agents respond to prompts. The system is intended to eliminate conflicting definitions that can cause AI agents to produce incorrect results.
The new capability addresses a problem the company encountered as customers began deploying its Aida natural-language data assistant in production environments, said Starburst co-founder and Chief Executive Justin Borgman.
“We’ve found that as you get into production, the biggest issue is context because you need to trust the answers the agent gives back,” he said.

articles.title: Travail et IA : ces métiers où les offres d'emploi se sont effondrées
articles.summary:
Derrière les fantasmes de remplacement par des robots, la réalité autour de l’intelligence artificielle et du marché du travail s’avère plus subtile, mais bien réelle. Deux études récentes, menées par France Travail auprès de 16 000 établissements et par le cabinet Coface, révèlent les vraies tendances du marché. Si les patrons privilégient pour l’instant le gain de productivité plutôt que les suppressions de postes, les embauches reculent déjà dans les professions tertiaires.
Des secteurs plus touchés que d’autres par l’IA
Selon France Travail, seuls 6 % des dirigeants prévoient une automatisation importante où l’IA exécuterait la majorité des tâches humaines d’ici cinq ans. En revanche, 35 % des patrons considèrent cette technologie comme un assistant de travail, capable de libérer du temps sur la rédaction, la recherche ou l’analyse. Parmi les métiers les plus touchés, on compte ceux du numérique et des services intellectuels, avec 94 % des ingénieurs informatiques, 83 % des comptables et 75 % des bancassureurs concernés. À l’inverse, le BTP (80 % sans effet), les services aux particuliers (85 %) et la restauration (76 %) ne sont que très peu touchés.
D’après l’étude, cette transition vers l’IA se concentre fortement dans les grandes agglomérations comme l’Île-de-France, le Rhône, la Loire-Atlantique ou la Haute-Garonne. Dans ces bassins d’emploi tertiaires, l’IA générative prend par exemple en charge les tâches administratives répétitives et la saisie de texte ou de donné…

La falla, registrada como CVE-2026-114938, está en una función de OpenJDK que procesa información codificada en Base64, un formato habitual en inicios de sesión, cargas de archivos e intercambios de datos entre servicios. En determinadas condiciones, un atacante podría provocar la exposición de información almacenada en la memoria de una aplicación o ejecutar código de forma remota.
El problema fue divulgado el 17 de noviembre y Oracle publicó parches de seguridad para las versiones afectadas. La vulnerabilidad puede alcanzar sistemas empresariales que usan Java, entre ellos plataformas de gestión, servidores y herramientas de autenticación. Sin embargo, no hay reportes públicos de ataques que ya hayan aprovechado esta falla.
La actualización de Java corresponde a las empresas que administran los sistemas
Para una persona que usa una aplicación bancaria, una billetera digital o un servicio de salud, la corrección técnica no depende de instalar manualmente Java en el celular. El parche debe aplicarlo la organización que opera los servidores y las aplicaciones afectadas.

articles.title: Windows Server 2028 trades compatibility for out-of-the-box security
articles.summary:
Microsoft’s Ignite announcements this week went beyond the Office-in-Copilot overhaul with the reveal of the Windows Server 2028 Public Preview and its new security-by-default stance and what Microsoft calls Hardened Server Core. Windows Server 2028 will implement a default security framework that Microsoft says is aligned with hardened DoD benchmarks, such as the Defense Information Systems Agency’s (DISA) Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG).
STIGs work by providing a standard security framework for system administrators to follow recommended guidance. In the past, Windows Server admins were left to start from a blank canvas and then implement hardening configurations for operations. Secure baselines were available but not the default. Microsoft says that concern is now managed: “The secure configuration is the starting state, not a project you run after setup. That closes the window where a newly deployed server sits exposed while it waits to be hardened.”
The new Windows Server 2028 hardened-by-default state will only be available for the Server Core installs. Windows Server Desktop Experience installs do not include the changed stance.
This isn’t to say that system administrators won’t still have the final say on which security protocols are activated, just that the default package now ships in a pre-hardened state. Por meio do novo aplicativo, os usuários podem armazenar e acessar determinados tipos de documentos no Google Wallet, como passagens aéreas, ingressos para shows e cartões de fidelidade.

articles.title: AI is now finding bugs in the code that runs banks, airlines, and hospitals

The takeaway: An AI model built for security research has uncovered a series of vulnerabilities in Java, the Oracle programming language used in the systems of airlines, banks, hospitals, and government agencies. The flaws were discovered by cybersecurity startup Calif using OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber model. Now, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency urged companies to update every system running Java.
Oracle released what it called a "critical security patch update" the same day and urged customers to install it. The company declined to comment further. Applying the fix could be a major undertaking: 90% of Fortune 500 companies use Java, which is deeply embedded in the software that keeps large organizations running.
Bruce Dang, a senior researcher at Calif, said the language's widespread use is what makes the discovery so serious. "Java is basically critical infrastructure," he told The Financial Times. "It's so central to the technology that we depend on . . . [and] a lot of big companies are going to have their work cut out to get it fixed."
Calif said it notified Oracle about the vulnerability last month. It then worked with government agencies through the Five Eyes intelligence-sharing alliance, which includes Australia, Canada, New Zealand, the UK and the US. Amazon, Apple, Google, and Microsoft also helped coordinate fixes. articles.summary:
Nvidia GeForce driver bug reportedly hammers SSDs with up to 30GB of writes per hour — users trace massive idle wear to background service, newer driver reportedly still affected
That would use up to 5% of a typical 1TB SSD’s rated endurance each year.
Nvidia’s GeForce driver 621.14 is reportedly causing excessive background writes on idle PCs, inducing extra wear on SSDs. One user measured about 3GB an hour on the susceptible driver, and another mentioned estimated up to 30GB/hour on the newer 621.24. This follows a similar-looking bug from AMD’s video driver discovered last month.
The bug is described by user Andergraude in an Nvidia forum post as “new in 621.14,” which came out on Nov. 4, who says it operates by “continuously [rewriting] the binary log file” with “real writes” to the drive. The writes are coming from the NVDisplay.Container.exe process, or the “NVIDIA Display Container LS” service, which logs to the nvlog.nvlgstg file. This background service is necessary for running the Nvidia Control Panel and App. It’s not clear what’s written in the log, and not every system is necessarily impacted.
The “real writes” point comes from the fact that a per-process write counter is not the same as writes reaching the drive. The measurements came from Windows Resource Monitor, Windows performance counters, and CrystalDiskInfo. The Data Units Written counter matched Windows’ reporting. Drug researchers and medical laboratories generate massive volumes of biological data every single day, yet somehow the artificial intelligence models designed to speed up drug discovery are still starved of useful information.
It’s a strange paradox, but a startup called Tesorai Inc. believes it has the solution after raising $5.3 million in seed funding today.
The round was led by Perplexity Fund, IQT and South Central Ventures, and saw New Stack Ventures, NextGen Venture Partners, f7 Ventures, VitalStage Ventures and ZAKA participating. With its completion, Tesorai has now raised $8 million in total, and will use that money to try to accelerate AI-driven scientific discovery by digging deeper into existing datasets to surface the deeply buried insights that human researchers have missed.
Biological data covers a broad spectrum spanning genetic sequences to protein measurements, and metabolomic processes to cellular imaging. This information is extremely valuable to drug researchers, because it serves as the primary fuel for training advanced AI models that can predict disease pathways and identify new therapies.

Les vues YouTube sur TV vont parfois compter double, ou triple
Depuis le 16 novembre, YouTube a changé une nouvelle fois de manière de comptabiliser les vues : « nous allons franchir une nouvelle étape dans la mesure de la façon dont les spectateurs regardent vos contenus sur les téléviseurs », peut-on lire sur le forum dédié aux créateurs sur la plateforme. YouTube intègre dans le compteur de vues d’une vidéo les estimations de covisionnage, jusque-là cantonnées dans les statistiques de chaque chaîne YouTube. Autrement dit, lorsque YouTube estimera que plusieurs personnes regardent une même vidéo sur un même téléviseur, ce ne sera plus une seule vue qui sera comptabilisée, mais plusieurs.
YouTube revendique officiellement qu’il s’agit de refléter « plus précisément la façon dont les spectateurs regardent vos contenus. » Mais c’est aussi un moyen de faire gonfler les vues d’une vidéo et ainsi de renforcer son attractivité commerciale ou encore d’encourager les créateurs et les internautes à rester sur la plateforme grâce à cet effet de preuve sociale. Une partie de ces titres vient de billets convertibles, et aucun ne donne de droit de vote. Anthropic et ses cofondateurs pourraient lever jusqu’à 64,4 milliards de dollars.
Anthropic doit fixer le prix de son action ce mercredi 18 novembre, avant une cotation jeudi sur le Nasdaq sous le symbole “ANT”. Les derniers documents d’Anthropic, repris par Bloomberg, précisent ce que deux de ses fournisseurs cloud vont détenir.
Actions sans vote et billets convertibles : comment Amazon et Google entrent au capital

articles.title: NASA's Voyager 1 reaches a distance of one light-day from Earth
articles.summary:
In a nutshell: NASA's Voyager 1 has become the first human-made object to travel one light-day from Earth. The milestone occurred on November 18 at 5:16:07 a.m. Eastern time, roughly nine years before its twin spacecraft, Voyager 2, will achieve the same feat.
One "day" might not sound like a lot of time or distance, and in the vast emptiness of space, where everything is so far apart, it really isn't. Rather than using familiar measurements such as miles or kilometers, distances in space are often described in terms of how light travels.
Light moves through space at approximately 186,000 miles per second, and nothing travels faster. The Moon, for reference, is roughly 238,855 miles from Earth on average, and it takes light about 1.3 seconds to travel that distance. At 93 million miles away, sunlight takes about eight minutes and 20 seconds to reach our planet. Astronomers also use the latter, called an astronomical unit (or AU for short), as a unit of length in space.
As you might have guessed, a light-day is the distance light travels in 24 hours: 16,094,799,096 miles (25,902,068,356 kilometers), to be exact. A light-year, by comparison, is roughly 5.88 trillion miles.
NASA launched the two Voyager probes in 1977 to study planets in the outskirts of our solar system, including gas giants Jupiter and Saturn. Voyager 1, which lifted off on September 5, completed its planetary objectives and entered into an extended mission phase in 1980. Voyager 2 launched a couple of weeks e…

Quantum computing drops its decade-away tag as error rates fall 200-fold in two years
Quantum computing is shedding its reputation as speculative as gains in quantum error correction turn fragile machines into reliable ones. For the supercomputing community, which now measures data centers in gigawatts of power, the more pressing question is how quantum fits beside the processors already on the floor.
For years, the field faced a trade-off between speed and reliability, because correcting errors inside a quantum computer slowed it down. That trade-off is fading fast, according to Rajeeb Hazra (pictured), chief executive officer of Quantinuum Inc., which listed on the Nasdaq in June.
“We are now at a stage in 2026 where we have the ability to have tremendous amounts of computation at a very high reliability rate,” Hazra said. “Just two weeks ago, we announced we were doing up to a million operations with five errors. To put it in contrast, just two years ago, we were trying to do 1,000 operations with one error. That’s how fast it is.”
Hazra spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Gemma Allen at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed advances in quantum error correction and how AI and quantum computing work in tandem. (* Disclosure below.)

Un incident survenu récemment a prouvé à quel point les satellites sont vulnérables, alors que l’engin russe Kosmos 2612 s’est dangereusement rapproché d’un dispositif occidental. Le besoin de sécuriser les satellites est désormais primordial, à tel point que le Royaume-Uni a commandé un essaim de « gardes du corps » pour protéger ses systèmes en orbite. C’est maintenant au tour de l’OTAN d’entrer en scène.
Des satellites exposés
Ce 17 novembre, lors de la conférence NATO EDGE 26 d’Izmir en Turquie, l’instance a dévoilé deux initiatives : Starlift et la Global Data Marketplace. Leur point commun : s’appuyer davantage sur les entreprises privées pour accéder à l’espace, qui est considéré comme l’un de ses domaines opérationnels depuis 2019, indique Bloomberg.
Car l’Alliance possède de nombreux satellites assurant les communications, la navigation, le renseignement et la défense antimissile. Or, ces derniers sont exposés au brouillage de leurs signaux et aux cyberattaques. Dans ce contexte, la plateforme Starlift doit regrouper les besoins militaires des pays participants et leur réserver des places sur des fusées commerciales, à la manière d’un courtier. AI’s hidden energy tax: More than 80% of scale-up traffic is just memory moving around
Memory bottlenecks are emerging as one of the costliest problems in AI infrastructure as inference overtakes training. GPUs sit idle waiting on data, while high-bandwidth memory, or HBM, stays bolted to processors that cannot share it.
Photonics is shaping up as one way out. Marvell Technology Inc. has been pairing optics with photonic memory to stretch memory beyond the edge of a chip. The payoff is better efficiency in data centers enterprises have already paid for, according to Preet Virk (pictured, left), senior vice president and general manager of the Photonic Fabric Business Unit at Marvell.
“In the data center today, we have a lot of room for improvement of efficiency,” Virk said. “And when I say efficiency, I’m alluding to the wasted flops because we have GPU utilization that’s very low.”
Virk and Andy Mills (right), vice president of advanced product development at Penguin Solutions Inc., spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Amit Eyal Govrin at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how photonics and shared memory pools can ease memory bottlenecks in AI infrastructure. (* Disclosure below.)

articles.title: La Macif écope d'une amende de 5 millions d'euros : les mots de passe étaient laissés à la merci des pirates

La Cnil, soit le gendarme des données personnelles, a annoncé une amende de cinq millions d’euros infligée à une société qui n’a pas été nommée. Cependant, selon les informations de BFMT Tech, il s’agit de la Macif, la société de groupe d’assurance mutuelle. Pourquoi une telle amende ? Lors d’un contrôle, la Cnil a constaté deux manquements importants au RGPD, le règlement européen sur les données personnelles.
Des mots de passe stockés en clair et des données conservées pendant plus de 10 ans
Avant toute chose, précisons que la Cnil a anonymisé la société qui s’est vue infliger une amende de cinq millions d’euros, car elle voulait que sa délibération soit publiée « à des fins pédagogiques ». En fin de compte, il semble y avoir peu de doute quant à l’identité de cette société. En effet, BFM Tech a contacté la Macif, qui reconnaît être concernée et « prend acte » de la décision de la Cnil.
Qu’est-il reproché à la Macif ? D’une part, l’entreprise française a stocké en clair les mots de passe de ses clients et leurs réponses aux questions de sécurité, sans aucune protection donc. Selon BFM Tech, 1,8 million de mots de passe étaient stockés en clair. Les identifiants, adresses e-mail et mots de passe étaient par ailleurs partagés sur des plateformes non sécurisées. Un employé de la société pouvait donc avoir accès à ces données confidentielles simplement en accédant à l’une de ces plateformes. The conversation is moving from theoretical potential toward practical application
For the past decade, success in quantum computing has been measured through research breakthroughs, investment, and technical milestones. This is beginning to change. Across industries, organizations are focusing on viable quantum solutions, shifting the conversation from theoretical potential towards practical application.
This acceleration presents a strategic challenge for governments. As commercial markets increasingly focus on real-world use cases, there is a risk that governments’ ability to adopt quantum technologies will fail to keep pace. Businesses can experiment with emerging technologies in quick iterations, but governments must navigate long procurement cycles and stringent internet security requirements.
This challenge is compounded by the need for governments to identify priority use cases and communicate them to the commercial market at an appropriate level of sensitivity. Without sufficient visibility into these requirements, systems may be developed in ways that do not align with, or are not appropriate for, government use cases.

articles.title: Bill Gates cuenta cómo Guinea utilizó tecnología para combatir una enfermedad transmitida por una mosca mortal
articles.summary:
Bill Gates expone el trabajo de Mamadou Camara para combatir la enfermedad del sueño en zonas costeras de Guinea.
La tecnología no siempre requiere equipos electrónicos sofisticados o sistemas de inteligencia artificial. En ocasiones, una solución sencilla puede cambiar la vida de miles de personas. Así lo demuestra la historia que compartió Bill Gates en su blog Gates Notes, donde relata cómo Guinea utilizó herramientas de control de insectos, métodos de investigación sanitaria y avances farmacológicos para combatir una enfermedad transmitida por la mosca tse-tsé.
El protagonista de esta historia es Mamadou Camara, un especialista en salud pública que dedicó más de 30 años a investigar y combatir la tripanosomiasis africana humana, conocida popularmente como enfermedad del sueño.
Esta infección es causada por un parásito que llega al organismo mediante la picadura de una mosca tse-tsé infectada. En sus primeras etapas puede provocar fiebre, dolores de cabeza y cansancio. Sin tratamiento, puede alcanzar el sistema nervioso central y generar alteraciones del comportamiento, confusión, trastornos del sueño y, finalmente, la muerte.
Las trampas tecnológicas que ayudaron a combatir la mosca tse-tsé
Cuando Camara comenzó sus investigaciones en 1992, uno de los principales problemas era identificar los lugares donde se concentraban los insectos transmisores. Para conseguirlo, su equipo recorrió distintas regiones de Guinea y recopiló información sobre los contagios.

Aunque muchas personas consideran que utilizar ambos equipos aumenta el gasto de electricidad, los expertos señalan que esta combinación permite distribuir mejor el aire frío y evitar que el sistema de climatización trabaje a temperaturas demasiado bajas.
El ingeniero Daniel Beguería, citado por el El Español, explica que no es necesario elegir entre uno de estos aparatos. Por el contrario, utilizarlos de manera conjunta puede mejorar el confort dentro de una habitación y disminuir la exigencia sobre el aire acondicionado.
La explicación está relacionada con la manera en que el cuerpo humano percibe el calor. Un ventilador no reduce la temperatura del ambiente, pero genera una corriente de aire que favorece la evaporación del sudor y ayuda a disipar el calor corporal. Esto permite sentir mayor frescura incluso cuando el termómetro registra temperaturas elevadas.
Una habitación puede resultar confortable a 28 o 30 grados cuando existe una circulación adecuada del aire, sin necesidad de mantener el aire acondicionado a temperaturas considerablemente más bajas.

articles.title: Researchers Claim Two RCE Exploits That Bypass Telegram’s New Android Defenses
articles.summary:
A malicious widget can bypass the security filter that Telegram added to its Android app last week and run code outside it, according to NebuSec, a security company.
Widgets are small interactive blocks that bots send inside chat messages, and their JavaScript runs on the user's phone. The researchers ran their demonstration on a Telegram test server, because only approved bots can send widgets on the live service now.
Bots could start sending widgets last week. Two days later, an account called V12 posted a video on X claiming that any Telegram message could now be used to execute remote code.
Telegram then put QuickJS, the small engine that runs widget JavaScript, into its own process on Android. It also added a seccomp filter, which can block or record the system calls that the process makes. Both changes appear in the source code it published for Telegram for Android 13.2.2 (7303).
NebuSec said in a technical analysis published earlier this week that its researchers got code running outside that filter in two separate ways. One uses a widget bug the filter does not cover, and the other chains a widget bug the filter does cover with a kernel bug.
In their video, a bot's Telegram widget on Android 13.2.2 (7303) bypasses the filter and opens the phone's calculator app, the researchers say.
Their write-up and their demonstration post on X do not say what the code could reach beyond that, such as the app's messages or the rest of the phone. They also do not say whether the use…

Sony Defeats UK PlayStation Store Lawsuit With Help From Physical Discs
London's Competition Appeal Tribunal (CAT) unanimously dismissed the £1.97 billion ($2.6 billion) class action lawsuit against Sony on November 17, according to The Game Business. As a result, 12.2 million UK PlayStation users won't receive a payout. The claim was filed by consumer rights advocate Alex Neill in August 2022, accusing Sony of abusing a near-monopoly over digital PlayStation games and add-ons. He added that Sony funnels every purchase through the PlayStation Store, where it takes a 30% commission. articles.summary:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has urged organizations to immediately patch a newly disclosed critical security flaw impacting Oracle Java.
The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-114938 (CVSS score: 8.1), refers to a case of out-of-bounds write that can lead to denial-of-service (DoS) or remote code execution under certain conditions.
"This critical memory-corruption vulnerability, known as 'Java4Shell,' affects the Base64 decoder of the x86-64 HotSpot Java Virtual Machine (JVM), which is part of the Java Development Kit (JDK)," CISA said. "Specially crafted Base64 input could crash the JVM and allow for unauthenticated remote code execution."
Patches for the flaw have been released by Oracle and OpenJDK. As of writing, there is no evidence the vulnerability has been exploited in the wild.
As reported previously by The Hacker News, Java4Shell can enable attackers without an account to execute arbitrary code on Keycloak, Atlassian Jira, Atlassian Confluence, JFrog Artifactory, Jenkins, and PingFederate, and with a login on Apache Kafka Broker, Apache Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit, and Spinnaker, under default settings.
Advisories for the flaw have been released by numerous security and software vendors, including Aikido, Amazon Linux, Blackpoint Cyber, Chainguard, Cisco Talos, Cycode, Datadog, Dynatrace, Endor Labs, Field Effect, Hadrian, Horizon3.ai, Miggo, Orca Security, Qualys, Rapid7, Red Hat, SentinelOne, Sophos, Tanium, Tenable, Upwind, VulnCheck, …

articles.title: GTA 6 Reportedly Plays Best on PS5 Pro, Xbox Series S Struggles
articles.summary:
Wednesday, November 18th 2026
GTA 6 Reportedly Plays Best on PS5 Pro, Xbox Series S Struggles
Digital Foundry has published its detailed platform comparison for GTA 6 based on over 100 hours of testing. Rockstar has officially confirmed that every console targets 30 FPS, and even the PS5 Pro misses out on a 40 FPS or 60 FPS mode. The PS5 Pro, PS5, and Xbox Series X all render at 1440p, but only the PS5 Pro reconstructs that into a 4K-like image using PSSR. The other two get a softer spatial upscale through Rockstar's own TAA. The Pro is also the only version with ray-traced shadows, while the other consoles have to make do with RT global illumination and RT reflections only. 
In DF's technical analysis, the PS5 Pro was able to hold 30 FPS across roughly 75 hours of play, briefly dropping to 24 FPS in scenes with intense explosions. The base PS5 and Xbox Series X bounce between 30 FPS and the high 20s during combat and fast traversal, but they can also dip into the low 20s in very intense scenes. DF notes that the Xbox Series X feels slightly smoother thanks to Xbox's 120 Hz VRR container. The PlayStation does not benefit from VRR at all, since it only kicks in above 48 FPS. Still, Digital Foundry's verdict is that both versions look and play well. Then there's the Xbox Series S…Xbox's "little brother" console is the hardest to recommend for Grand Theft Auto 6. articles.title: Comment libérer de l’espace sur son PC avec ChatGPT ou Claude
articles.summary:
Avant de désinstaller un jeu ou de vous lancer dans le tri de vos photos, demandez à ChatGPT ou à Claude ce qui encombre votre PC. Sur le nôtre, une démo avait laissé à elle seule près de 60 Go de fichiers dont on pouvait se passer.
On sait assez bien ce qui prend de la place sur un PC qu’on vient de monter ou d’acheter. Quelques années et quelques dizaines d’installations plus tard, on a une idée beaucoup plus vague de ce qui se cache sur le SSD. Au moment de faire le ménage, c’est souvent un jeu qui en fait les frais, pour la simple raison qu’on sait où le trouver et combien sa désinstallation va rapporter. On pense moins volontiers aux fichiers qu’un logiciel a mis de côté pour gagner du temps la prochaine fois qu’on l’ouvrira. C’est pourtant là qu’on a fait la plus belle trouvaille de cet essai.
L’idée nous est venue en demandant à Hermes, notre agent IA, de regarder ce qui remplissait le disque. Il nous avait proposé plusieurs lots de fichiers à nettoyer, en expliquant pour chacun ce qu’on pouvait gagner et ce qu’on risquait de perdre. On a voulu voir si l’on pouvait obtenir le même coup de main avec ChatGPT, plus accessible qu’Hermes. articles.title: Hackers Exploiting Critical Puppet RCE Flaw Affecting Enterprise Management Servers
articles.summary:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Tuesday added a critical security flaw impacting Perforce Puppet, an enterprise infrastructure-as-code (IaC) and configuration management platform, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing reports of active exploitation.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-115731 (CVSS score: 9.4), is a case of deserialization of untrusted data that could result in remote code execution.
"Perforce Puppet Enterprise contains a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability in Puppet's report-processing code that allows a client with any CA-signed agent certificate to execute arbitrary code on the Puppet Server as the service user by submitting a report containing a crafted rich-data type through a PUT request," CISA said.
"If the certificate authority automatically signs requests without strong verification, an unauthenticated network attacker can obtain a valid certificate and exploit the vulnerability."
The shortcoming impacts the following versions -
- Puppet Enterprise 2026.0.0 before 2026.0.1
- Puppet Enterprise 2025.0.0 before 2025.12.1
- Puppet Enterprise 2023.8.0 before 2023.8.13
- Puppet Core 9.0.0 before 9.1.3
- Puppet Core 8.x before 8.22.2
It was addressed by Perforce Software on November 3, 2026, in the following versions -
- Puppet Enterprise 2026.0.1 (Puppet Core 9.1.3)

articles.title: Quality Isn’t The Main Worry About AI Pentesting — Data Privacy and Production Safety Are
articles.summary:
AI is speeding up how software is built, which means more code, more changes, and more chances for vulnerabilities to reach production. It's speeding up how attackers find and exploit them too, with time-to-exploit now down to a single day. Security testing has to keep up with both.
AI pentesting has emerged as a way to run in-depth tests whenever teams need them, instead of waiting for the next scheduled pentest. To see how far adoption has come and what security teams need from it, Intruder surveyed 500 security and engineering leaders across the US and UK. Read on for the top findings.
Only 4% of security leaders believe their current testing frequency gives them sufficient coverage
68% of organizations deploy code to production at least daily, and 37% deploy multiple times a day. Understandably, pentesting runs on a much slower cycle. Nearly half (47%) go more than a month between full pentests on their web applications and APIs. Those figures are for each organization's most frequently tested application, so the rest of their estate is tested less often still.
Running a human-led pentest as often as code ships has never been realistic, largely because of the cost. But it means a vulnerability introduced in one release can go weeks or months without a pentest, and only 4% of security leaders believe their current testing frequency gives them sufficient coverage.

articles.title: Java4Shell Flaw (CVE-2026-114938) Enables Pre-Auth RCE in Jira, Jenkins, Keycloak and More
articles.summary:
A Java flaw called Java4Shell can let attackers without an account run their own code on Jira, Jenkins, Keycloak, and three other widely used applications, says Calif, the security research firm that disclosed it this week.
The flaw is present in Java 17.0.6 and later, and the vulnerable code runs only on x86-64 Intel and AMD chips that support the AVX-512 VBMI feature.
Tracked as CVE-2026-114938, the fix was released today by Oracle and the OpenJDK project, whose open-source code underpins Java builds from many vendors. Amazon has fixed its Corretto Java builds, but Red Hat is still preparing fixes for its own.
The researchers are holding back their attack code for the six applications, and other labs have so far reproduced crashes and a memory leak but not the code execution. Canada's Cyber Center said this week that it was not aware of any attacks exploiting the flaw.
Servers often decode Base64-encoded data, such as HTTP Basic login headers, SAML artifacts, and CSRF tokens, before checking whether a user is logged in. That is how an attacker without an account can exploit the flaw.
The flaw is in a faster version of Java's Base64 decoder that runs on chips with AVX-512 VBMI. Java switches to it after compiling the decoder for speed, which it does for code that runs often.
A malformed string that ends with an extra = makes this decoder write 62 or 63 bytes past the end of its output. Java rejects the string, but only after the write.

Android Authority has found text strings in code for Google’s SIM Manager app that suggest a new feature called Android Fast Switch is in the works, and that this is designed to let you seamlessly use one number on two different handsets, as long as both are signed into the same Google account.
It sounds a lot like Apple’s recently launched iPhone Handoff feature, which lets you share one number between two different iPhones. Though that feature only works with eSIMs, and currently only on a few carriers, such as T-Mobile in the US and EE in the UK.
Limited compatibility

Sin embargo, la compra exige una suscripción mensual para que el vehículo pueda circular y restringe su operación a zonas autorizadas por la empresa.
Cuál es el vehículo sin volante ni pedales de Tesla
El Cybercab, presentado por Tesla en octubre de 2024, es un vehículo de dos plazas concebido para desplazarse de manera autónoma. No cuenta con volante, pedales ni otros mandos destinados a la conducción convencional, así que sus dueños no disponen de una alternativa manual si el sistema autónomo deja de estar disponible.
Sumado al precio de compra, los usuarios deben contratar una suscripción de autonomía de USD 299 al mes. Los términos del servicio establecen que el vehículo no funcionará sin una suscripción activa. El primer mes está incluido, pero posteriormente el cobro se renueva de forma mensual.

articles.summary:
La plus petite des Xbox calcule GTA 6 en 720p et s’appuie sur l’IA pour reconstruire une image en 1080p. Sur Xbox Series X et PS5, Rockstar part de 1440p et confie la mise à l’échelle vers la 4K à sa propre technologie.

articles.title: New Attack Bypasses TPM Lockout to Crack Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs in Days, Not Years
articles.summary:
On AMD-based PCs and some Intel PCs, the TPM lockout for Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs can be reset by someone who opens the PC's case, researchers at Technische Universität Berlin say.
That leaves short PINs open to guessing. In lab tests, the researchers found a four-digit Hello PIN on an AMD laptop and a 6-digit BitLocker PIN on an Intel laptop this way.
Both PINs were set by the researchers and found within 236 tries. From the speeds they measured, they calculate a worst-case of 40 hours for a four-digit Hello PIN, compared to 69 days with the lockout working as documented. For a default six-digit BitLocker PIN, the worst-case time drops from 19 years to 20 days.
AMD confirmed yesterday that its processor firmware has a flaw that allows the attack on some PCs with its chips. It plans fixes for most of those chips between November and February 2027. For now, the researchers advise adding at least two digits to Hello and BitLocker PINs.
The TPM in these PCs is a firmware TPM, built into the processor. Unlike a separate TPM chip, it has no secure storage of its own, according to the research paper the researchers posted late last week. So it keeps its saved state, including the count of wrong guesses, encrypted on the mainboard's flash chip.
If someone copies that saved state and later writes the old copy back, the count goes back too, unless the PC detects it. Newer PCs try to catch this with counters inside the flash chip, called RPMC, that can only go up.

A critical security flaw in Apache Roller, an open-source, Java-based blogging platform, has come under active exploitation in the wild, according to the Apache Software Foundation (ASF)
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-129448 (CVSS score: 9.8), is a case of unauthenticated deserialization in the XML-RPC endpoint that could lead to remote code execution.
"Deserialization of Untrusted Data in Apache Roller versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code," project maintainers said. "The XML-RPC endpoint accepts vendor extension types and deserializes them before authenticating the requester."
ASF also noted that the vulnerability is the same as CVE-2026-82384 (CVSS score: 9.8), which was patched in September 2026 and listed only Apache Roller 6.1.5 as affected.
"This issue is being actively exploited," it added. ASF did not share any details on how the vulnerability is being exploited, or who is being targeted as part of these efforts.
A security researcher named n0mi1k has been credited with finding the flaw, and Matt Raible has been acknowledged for reporting it.
Users are advised to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later, which disables the extension types and rejects XML-RPC requests when the XML-RPC feature is disabled.
If immediate patching is not an option, it's recommended to set "enabledForExtensions" to "false" in WEB-INF/web.xml, or remove the "/roller-services/xmlrpc" servlet mapping, and then restart Roller.

Six critical vulnerabilities in F5 BIG-IP allow an attacker to crash the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) without logging in, disrupting traffic until the TMM restarts.
Each flaw needs a specific setup on a virtual server: an iRule that uses a particular command, or an APM policy that includes two particular kinds of agent.
F5, which makes BIG-IP, disclosed the flaws today and says they may also allow remote code execution. The company has released engineering hotfixes and lists no workaround.
The company rates all six 9.8 under CVSS v3.1 and 9.3 under CVSS v4.0. They are stack-based buffer overflows in BIG-IP's data plane, the part that processes almost all of its network traffic. The management side is not exposed, according to the company.
None of the company's advisories says the flaws have been exploited. WatchTowr researcher Sina Kheirkhah reported four, and the company found the other two itself.
Five of the flaws are in iRules, a BIG-IP feature that administrators use to manage traffic, and one is in BIG-IP's APM module. Some also affect BIG-IP Next for Kubernetes and BIG-IP CNF, part of the company's BIG-IP Cloud-Native Edition.
Each flaw needs the setup listed below on a virtual server:
- CVE-2026-123637: an APM per-request policy that includes both the Client Information agent and Endpoint Security agents. Affects BIG-IP APM only.

articles.title: Voltage glitch unlocks 80GB on Nvidia's CMP 170HX, but 'faster than an A100' rests on a single benchmark
articles.summary:
Voltage glitch unlocks 80GB on Nvidia's CMP 170HX, but 'faster than an A100' rests on a single benchmark
Nvidia built the CMP 170HX to be a worse A100
- Researcher uses voltage fault injection on Nvidia's GA100 die to blow normally locked fuses and re-enable memory and compute on the crippled CMP 170HX mining card
- An 8GB card can be pushed to a full 80GB of HBM and 120 to 126 working SMs, more than the 108 Nvidia currently enables on a retail A100
- The "faster than an A100" claim, however, rests on a single FP16 benchmark and leaves tensor performance, ECC, NVLink, and MIG untested or incomplete
Nvidia spent the better part of a decade teaching its silicon to keep secrets from its own owners, but a new piece of hardware research argues that, on at least one chip, those secrets were only ever a power glitch away.
Writing on her personal blog, a researcher known as Kate published a voltage fault injection attack on Nvidia's GA100, the Ampere die at the heart of the A100 data center accelerator.
Her claim is blunt but one backed by proof: by disrupting the chip's power delivery at the right moment during boot, she can write fuses that Nvidia designed to be unwritable, and in doing so re-enable the memory and compute the company switched off at the factory, resulting in a card that behaves as an 80GB A100, assembled from a mining accelerator that was never meant to be anything of that sort.
